issues: The original was scaled up from a 480×270 design space, so cards held initials and symbols only a dozen pixels tall and their content was unreadable
A light grey stage with multicoloured avatars and thumbnails; with so much colour the red cards competed with the thumbnails and the anomalies did not pop
Flagging just tinted the background pale red, with no sense of an event, and the title had nothing to do with the data on screen
It ended on the static grid with no landing
changes: Look = graphite: the whole wall is desaturated (avatars, logos and names in greyscale, healthy dots a muted grey-green) so the only saturated colour on screen is risk red
Re-laid out natively at 1920: 38 account cards at 200×118 (initials / abstract portrait / logo, 22px name, ARR) forming the account wall of a fictional customer-success product, Tether
Ring growth kept: ring number, 4f per ring plus 0–3f jitter, cards only fade, scale 0.86→1 with overshoot and come into focus, no travel

Flagging is an event: six well-spread cards turn red at uneven intervals across 52–101f, fill / border / dot on one curve plus a tick, a clipped red ripple and the ARR line swapping to a churn reason; the healthy cards dim 1→0.5

A 112px centre title 'Who's drifting away?' rises word by word, the 'n accounts · $Xk ARR at risk' summary and legend count up with each flag, and a red 'Bring them back in →' call-to-action pill rises for the end poster
A 1→1.03 slow camera push throughout, and a red glow behind the title that grows with the anomaly count
